sanskrit: aśvair viparidhāvadbhiḥ śaracchannair viśāṃ pate tatra tatra kṛto mārgo vikarṣadbhir hatān bahūn
english: By horses galloping wildly in every direction, riddled with arrows, O lord of the people, paths were carved here and there as they dragged along the many slain.

sanskrit: nihatānāṃ hayānāṃ ca sahaiva hayayodhibhiḥ varmabhir vinikṛttaiś ca prāsaiś chinnaiś ca māriṣa saṃchannā pṛthivī jajñe kusumaiḥ śabalā iva
english: With slaughtered horses together with their riders, with shattered coats of mail and broken lances, O venerable one, the earth became so covered that it seemed dappled, as if strewn with blossoms.

sanskrit: yodhās tatra mahārāja samāsādya parasparam vyacaranta raṇe kruddhā vinighnantaḥ parasparam
english: The warriors there, O great king, closing upon one another, ranged across the battlefield in fury, striking each other down.

sanskrit: udvṛttanayanai roṣāt saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭair mukhaiḥ sakuṇḍalair mahī channā padmakiñjalkasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: With faces whose eyes were rolled upward in rage and whose lips were bitten through, still wearing their earrings and resembling the filaments of lotuses, the earth was covered over.

sanskrit: bhujaiś chinnair mahārāja nāgarājakaropamaiḥ sāṅgadaiḥ satanutraiś ca sāsiprāsaparaśvadhaiḥ
english: With severed arms, O great king, that resembled the trunks of lordly elephants, still bearing their armlets and gauntlets and still grasping sword, lance, and battle-axe,

sanskrit: kabandhair utthitaiś chinnair nṛtyadbhiś cāparair yudhi kravyādagaṇasaṃkīrṇā ghorābhūt pṛthivī vibho
english: with headless trunks that had risen up though severed, and others dancing on the field, thronged with hosts of carrion-eaters, the earth became a thing of horror, O lord.

sanskrit: alpāvaśiṣṭe sainye tu kauraveyān mahāhave prahṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavā bhūtvā ninyire yamasādanam
english: When the army was reduced to a remnant, the Pāṇḍavas, grown exultant in that great battle, dispatched the Kauravas to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūraḥ saubaleyaḥ pratāpavān prāsena sahadevasya śirasi prāharad bhṛśam sa vihvalo mahārāja rathopastha upāviśat
english: In that interval the valiant, mighty son of Subala struck Sahadeva hard upon the head with a lance; and he, O great king, reeling and stunned, sank down upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān sarvasainyāni saṃkruddho vārayām āsa bhārata
english: Seeing Sahadeva thus, the mighty Bhīmasena, blazing with wrath, held back all the enemy hosts, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nirbibheda ca nārācaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ vinirbhidyākaroc caiva siṃhanādam ariṃdama
english: He pierced them through with iron shafts by the hundreds and the thousands, and having pierced them, he sent up a lion's roar, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastāḥ sarve sahayavāraṇāḥ prādravan sahasā bhītāḥ śakuneś ca padānugāḥ
english: Terrified by that sound, the followers of Śakuni, together with their horses and elephants, all at once fled in sudden fear.

sanskrit: prabhagnān atha tān dṛṣṭvā rājā duryodhano 'bravīt nivartadhvam adharmajñā yudhyadhvaṃ kiṃ sṛtena vaḥ
english: Seeing them broken in rout, King Duryodhana cried out: "Turn back, you who know not righteousness! Fight! What good is your flight to you?

sanskrit: iha kīrtiṃ samādhāya pretya lokān samaśnute prāṇāñ jahāti yo vīro yudhi pṛṣṭham adarśayan
english: The hero who wins renown here and yields up his life in battle without showing his back attains the higher worlds after death."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te rājñā saubalasya padānugāḥ pāṇḍavān abhyavartanta mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Thus addressed by the king, the followers of the son of Subala turned again upon the Pāṇḍavas, making death itself their refuge from retreat.

sanskrit: dravadbhis tatra rājendra kṛtaḥ śabdo 'tidāruṇaḥ kṣubdhasāgarasaṃkāśaḥ kṣubhitaḥ sarvato 'bhavat
english: By those rushing onward, O lord of kings, a most terrible roar was raised, like the tumult of a churning ocean, and it surged up on every side.

sanskrit: tāṃs tadāpatato dṛṣṭvā saubalasya padānugān pratyudyayur mahārāja pāṇḍavā vijaye vṛtāḥ
english: Beholding the followers of the son of Subala bearing down upon them, the Pāṇḍavas, intent upon victory, advanced to meet them, O great king.

sanskrit: pratyāśvasya ca durdharṣaḥ sahadevo viśāṃ pate śakuniṃ daśabhir viddhvā hayāṃś cāsya tribhiḥ śaraiḥ dhanuś ciccheda ca śaraiḥ saubalasya hasann iva
english: And the unassailable Sahadeva, having regained his breath, O lord of the people, pierced Śakuni with ten shafts and his horses with three, and as if smiling cut through the bow of the son of Subala with his arrows.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya śakunir yuddhadurmadaḥ vivyādha nakulaṃ ṣaṣṭyā bhīmasenaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Then taking up another bow, Śakuni, drunk with the frenzy of battle, pierced Nakula with sixty shafts and Bhīmasena with seven.

sanskrit: ulūko 'pi mahārāja bhīmaṃ vivyādha saptabhiḥ sahadevaṃ ca saptatyā parīpsan pitaraṃ raṇe
english: Ulūka too, O great king, seeking to shield his father in the fight, pierced Bhīma with seven shafts and Sahadeva with seventy.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ samare vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ śakuniṃ ca catuḥṣaṣṭyā pārśvasthāṃś ca tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Bhīmasena in that combat pierced him with sharpened shafts, and Śakuni with sixty-four, and those who stood at their flanks with three apiece.

sanskrit: te hanyamānā bhīmena nārācais tailapāyitaiḥ sahadevaṃ raṇe kruddhāś chādayañ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ savidyuta ivāmbudāḥ
english: Though struck by Bhīma with oil-tempered iron shafts, they in their wrath covered Sahadeva in battle with showers of arrows, as lightning-charged clouds drench a mountain with torrents of rain.

sanskrit: tato 'syāpatataḥ śūraḥ sahadevaḥ pratāpavān ulūkasya mahārāja bhallenāpāharac chiraḥ
english: Then, as Ulūka bore down upon him, the valiant and mighty Sahadeva struck off his head with a broad-headed shaft, O great king.

sanskrit: sa jagāma rathād bhūmiṃ sahadevena pātitaḥ rudhirāplutasarvāṅgo nandayan pāṇḍavān yudhi
english: Cast down by Sahadeva, he fell from his chariot to the ground, his every limb bathed in blood, gladdening the Pāṇḍavas in the battle.

sanskrit: putraṃ tu nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā śakunis tatra bhārata sāśrukaṇṭho viniḥśvasya kṣattur vākyam anusmaran
english: But seeing his son slain there, O Bhārata, Śakuni, his throat choked with tears, sighed deeply, recalling the words of Vidura.

sanskrit: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ sa bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇaḥ śvasan sahadevaṃ samāsādya tribhir vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Having brooded a moment, his eyes brimming with tears and sighing, he closed upon Sahadeva and pierced him with three arrows.

sanskrit: tān apāsya śarān muktāñ śarasaṃghaiḥ pratāpavān sahadevo mahārāja dhanuś ciccheda saṃyuge
english: Warding off those loosed shafts with volleys of his own arrows, the mighty Sahadeva, O great king, cut through his bow in the encounter.

sanskrit: chinne dhanuṣi rājendra śakuniḥ saubalas tadā pragṛhya vipulaṃ khaḍgaṃ sahadevāya prāhiṇot
english: His bow being severed, O lord of kings, Śakuni the son of Subala then seized a broad sword and hurled it at Sahadeva.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate dvidhā ciccheda samare saubalasya hasann iva
english: As that sword of dreadful form came rushing upon him, O lord of the people, he cut the weapon of the son of Subala in two in the fray, as if in mockery.

sanskrit: asiṃ dṛṣṭvā dvidhā chinnaṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām prāhiṇot sahadevāya sā moghā nyapatad bhuvi
english: Seeing his sword cleft in two, he took up a great mace and hurled it at Sahadeva; but it fell vainly to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahāghorāṃ kālarātrim ivodyatām preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ prati saubalaḥ
english: Then the son of Subala, blazing with rage, flung at the Pāṇḍava a most fearful spear, upraised like the Night of Doom.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ tridhā ciccheda samare sahadevo hasann iva
english: As it came hurtling upon him, Sahadeva, as if smiling, cut it in three with gold-adorned shafts upon the field.

sanskrit: sā papāta tridhā chinnā bhūmau kanakabhūṣaṇā śīryamāṇā yathā dīptā gaganād vai śatahradā
english: Severed in three, that gold-wrought spear fell to the earth, crumbling as it dropped, like a blazing flash of lightning falling from the sky.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā saubalaṃ ca bhayārditam dudruvus tāvakāḥ sarve bhaye jāte sasaubalāḥ
english: Seeing the spear struck down and the son of Subala stricken with fear, all your men, the son of Subala among them, fled as terror seized them.

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ mahad dhy āsīt pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ dhārtarāṣṭrās tataḥ sarve prāyaśo vimukhābhavan
english: Then a great shout went up from the Pāṇḍavas, radiant with the look of victory, and thereupon the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra for the most part turned their faces away.

sanskrit: tān vai vimanaso dṛṣṭvā mādrīputraḥ pratāpavān śarair anekasāhasrair vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Seeing them downcast, the valiant son of Mādrī held them back in the battle with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārakair guptaṃ pṛṣṭhair aśvair jaye dhṛtam āsasāda raṇe yāntaṃ sahadevo 'tha saubalam
english: Then Sahadeva fell upon the son of Subala in the fight as he rode away, guarded by the Gāndhāras and seated upon swift, fine-backed horses, bent upon victory.

sanskrit: svam aṃśam avaśiṣṭaṃ sa saṃsmṛtya śakuniṃ nṛpa rathena kāñcanāṅgena sahadevaḥ samabhyayāt adhijyaṃ balavat kṛtvā vyākṣipan sumahad dhanuḥ
english: Recalling that Śakuni remained as the share allotted to him, O king, Sahadeva bore down upon him in his gold-bodied chariot, having strung and drawn back his great bow with main force.

sanskrit: sa saubalam abhidrutya gṛdhrapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ bhṛśam abhyahanat kruddhas tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: Rushing upon the son of Subala, he struck him hard in his wrath with stone-whetted, vulture-feathered shafts, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ medhāvī nigṛhya smārayann iva kṣatradharme sthito bhūtvā yudhyasva puruṣo bhava
english: And the wise one, checking him as though to remind him, said: "Standing firm in the duty of a warrior, fight! Be a man!

sanskrit: yat tadā hṛṣyase mūḍha glahann akṣaiḥ sabhātale phalam adya prapadyasva karmaṇas tasya durmate
english: That gladness you felt then, you fool, when you cast the dice in the assembly hall — receive now the fruit of that deed, O evil-minded one!

sanskrit: nihatās te durātmāno ye 'smān avahasan purā duryodhanaḥ kulāṅgāraḥ śiṣṭas tvaṃ tasya mātulaḥ
english: Slain are those wicked men who once mocked us; Duryodhana, the firebrand of his line, remains, and you, his maternal uncle.

sanskrit: adya te vihaniṣyāmi kṣureṇonmathitaṃ śiraḥ vṛkṣāt phalam ivoddhṛtya laguḍena pramāthinā
english: Today I will strike off your head, churned from your shoulders by a razor-shaft, as one plucks down a fruit from a tree with a crushing cudgel."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja sahadevo mahābalaḥ saṃkruddho naraśārdūlo vegenābhijagāma ha
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, the mighty Sahadeva, that tiger among men, blazing with wrath, advanced upon him with a rush.

sanskrit: abhigamya tu durdharṣaḥ sahadevo yudhāṃ patiḥ vikṛṣya balavac cāpaṃ krodhena prahasann iva
english: Closing in, the unassailable Sahadeva, that lord of warriors, drew his bow with might, as if laughing in his anger,

sanskrit: śakuniṃ daśabhir viddhvā caturbhiś cāsya vājinaḥ chatraṃ dhvajaṃ dhanuś cāsya chittvā siṃha ivānadat
english: and having pierced Śakuni with ten shafts and his horses with four, and cut down his parasol, his banner, and his bow, he roared like a lion.

sanskrit: chinnadhvajadhanuśchatraḥ sahadevena saubalaḥ tato viddhaś ca bahubhiḥ sarvamarmasu sāyakaiḥ
english: His banner, bow, and parasol cut away by Sahadeva, the son of Subala was then pierced in all his vital points by many arrows.

sanskrit: tato bhūyo mahārāja sahadevaḥ pratāpavān śakuneḥ preṣayām āsa śaravṛṣṭiṃ durāsadām
english: Then once more, O great king, the valiant Sahadeva sent against Śakuni an irresistible shower of arrows.

sanskrit: tatas tu kruddhaḥ subalasya putro; mādrīsutaṃ sahadevaṃ vimarde prāsena jāmbūnadabhūṣaṇena; jighāṃsur eko 'bhipapāta śīghram
english: Then the son of Subala, in his fury, single-handed and seeking to slay Sahadeva, the son of Mādrī, swiftly rushed upon him in the press of battle with a gold-decked lance.

sanskrit: mādrīsutas tasya samudyataṃ taṃ; prāsaṃ suvṛttau ca bhujau raṇāgre bhallais tribhir yugapat saṃcakarta; nanāda coccais tarasājimadhye
english: At the forefront of the fight the son of Mādrī, with three broad-headed shafts at a single stroke, severed that upraised lance together with both his shapely arms, and shouted aloud, sweeping through the middle of the field.

sanskrit: tasyāśukārī susamāhitena; suvarṇapuṅkhena dṛḍhāyasena bhallena sarvāvaraṇātigena; śiraḥ śarīrāt pramamātha bhūyaḥ
english: Then, acting in an instant, with a well-aimed broad shaft of hard iron, gold-feathered and able to pierce every guard, he wrenched the head from his body.

sanskrit: śareṇa kārtasvarabhūṣitena; divākarābhena susaṃśitena hṛtottamāṅgo yudhi pāṇḍavena; papāta bhūmau subalasya putraḥ
english: His head struck off in battle by the Pāṇḍava with that gold-adorned, keen-whetted shaft bright as the sun, the son of Subala fell to the earth.

sanskrit: sa tacchiro vegavatā śareṇa; suvarṇapuṅkhena śilāśitena prāverayat kupitaḥ pāṇḍuputro; yat tat kurūṇām anayasya mūlam
english: That head, which was the very root of the ruin of the Kurus, the son of Pāṇḍu in his wrath sent flying with a swift, gold-feathered, stone-whetted shaft.

sanskrit: hṛtottamāṅgaṃ śakuniṃ samīkṣya; bhūmau śayānaṃ rudhirārdragātram yodhās tvadīyā bhayanaṣṭasattvā; diśaḥ prajagmuḥ pragṛhītaśastrāḥ
english: Beholding Śakuni with his head struck off, lying upon the earth, his limbs drenched with blood, your warriors, their spirit shattered by terror, fled in every direction, still grasping their weapons.

sanskrit: vipradrutāḥ śuṣkamukhā visaṃjñā; gāṇḍīvaghoṣeṇa samāhatāś ca bhayārditā bhagnarathāśvanāgāḥ; padātayaś caiva sadhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
english: Routed, their mouths dry, their senses gone, stunned by the twang of Gāṇḍīva and tormented by fear, their chariots, horses, and elephants broken, the foot-soldiers too, along with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, fled away.

sanskrit: tato rathāc chakuniṃ pātayitvā; mudānvitā bhārata pāṇḍaveyāḥ śaṅkhān pradadhmuḥ samare prahṛṣṭāḥ; sakeśavāḥ sainikān harṣayantaḥ
english: Then, having cast Śakuni down from his chariot, the sons of Pāṇḍu, filled with joy, O Bhārata, blew their conches in the battle in their exultation, gladdening their soldiers, with Keśava among them.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi sarve pratipūjayanto; hṛṣṭā bruvāṇāḥ sahadevam ājau diṣṭyā hato naikṛtiko durātmā; sahātmajo vīra raṇe tvayeti
english: And all of them, doing honor to Sahadeva, said to him in their gladness upon the field: "By good fortune, O hero, the deceitful and wicked one, together with his son, has been slain by you in battle."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ kruddhā mahārāja saubalasya padānugāḥ tyaktvā jīvitam ākrande pāṇḍavān paryavārayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O great king, the followers of the son of Subala, enraged and giving up their lives amid the wailing, hemmed in the Pāṇḍavas on every side.

sanskrit: tān arjunaḥ pratyagṛhṇāt sahadevajaye dhṛtaḥ bhīmasenaś ca tejasvī kruddhāśīviṣadarśanaḥ
english: Them Arjuna received in battle, bent upon Sahadeva's victory, and Bhīmasena too, blazing with energy, his aspect like that of an enraged venomous serpent.

sanskrit: śaktyṛṣṭiprāsahastānāṃ sahadevaṃ jighāṃsatām saṃkalpam akaron moghaṃ gāṇḍīvena dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The resolve of those who, spear, pike, and lance in hand, sought to slay Sahadeva, Dhanaṃjaya rendered vain with Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: pragṛhītāyudhān bāhūn yodhānām abhidhāvatām bhallaiś ciccheda bībhatsuḥ śirāṃsy api hayān api
english: The arms that grasped weapons, of the warriors who rushed forward, Bībhatsu cut away with broad-headed shafts, and their heads as well, and their horses too.

sanskrit: te hatāḥ pratyapadyanta vasudhāṃ vigatāsavaḥ tvaritā lokavīreṇa prahatāḥ savyasācinā
english: Struck down and bereft of life, they sank to the earth, swiftly smitten by Savyasācin, that hero of the world.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā dṛṣṭvā svabalasaṃkṣayam hataśeṣān samānīya kruddho rathaśatān vibho
english: Then King Duryodhana, beholding the destruction of his host, in his wrath, O lord, gathered together the hundreds of chariots that survived the slaughter,

sanskrit: kuñjarāṃś ca hayāṃś caiva pādātāṃś ca paraṃtapa uvāca sahitān sarvān dhārtarāṣṭra idaṃ vacaḥ
english: and the elephants and horses and foot-soldiers, O scorcher of foes; and the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke to them all assembled these words:

sanskrit: samāsādya raṇe sarvān pāṇḍavān sasuhṛdgaṇān pāñcālyaṃ cāpi sabalaṃ hatvā śīghraṃ nivartata
english: "Closing upon all the Pāṇḍavas in battle, together with their bands of friends, and the Pāñcāla prince too with his force, slay them and swiftly turn back."

sanskrit: tasya te śirasā gṛhya vacanaṃ yuddhadurmadāḥ pratyudyayū raṇe pārthāṃs tava putrasya śāsanāt
english: Receiving his word upon their heads, those drunk with the frenzy of battle advanced to meet the sons of Pṛthā in the fight, at your son's command.

sanskrit: tān abhyāpatataḥ śīghraṃ hataśeṣān mahāraṇe śarair āśīviṣākāraiḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samavākiran
english: As they who had survived the slaughter rushed swiftly forward in that great battle, the Pāṇḍavas covered them over with shafts shaped like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tat sainyaṃ bharataśreṣṭha muhūrtena mahātmabhiḥ avadhyata raṇaṃ prāpya trātāraṃ nābhyavindata pratiṣṭhamānaṃ tu bhayān nāvatiṣṭhata daṃśitam
english: That army, O best of the Bhāratas, was in a moment slain by those great-souled ones once it joined the battle, and found no protector; yet though it sought to stand firm, for fear it could not hold its ground, armored though it was.

sanskrit: aśvair viparidhāvadbhiḥ sainyena rajasā vṛte na prājñāyanta samare diśaś ca pradiśas tathā
english: With horses galloping wildly and the host wrapped in dust, neither the quarters nor the intermediate quarters could be discerned in the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tu pāṇḍavānīkān niḥsṛtya bahavo janāḥ abhyaghnaṃs tāvakān yuddhe muhūrtād iva bhārata tato niḥśeṣam abhavat tat sainyaṃ tava bhārata
english: Then many men, sallying forth from the Pāṇḍava ranks, struck down your men in the fight in but a moment, O Bhārata; and so that army of yours was left without a remnant, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyaḥ sametās tu tava putrasya bhārata ekādaśa hatā yuddhe tāḥ prabho pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ
english: The eleven full armies assembled for your son, O Bhārata — those, O lord, were slain in battle by the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: teṣu rājasahasreṣu tāvakeṣu mahātmasu eko duryodhano rājann adṛśyata bhṛśaṃ kṣataḥ
english: Amid those thousands of great-souled kings of your side, Duryodhana alone, O king, was seen, sorely wounded.

sanskrit: tato vīkṣya diśaḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā śūnyāṃ ca medinīm vihīnaḥ sarvayodhaiś ca pāṇḍavān vīkṣya saṃyuge
english: Then, gazing about him in all directions and seeing the earth made empty, bereft of all his warriors, and beholding the Pāṇḍavas in the field —

sanskrit: muditān sarvasiddhārthān nardamānān samantataḥ bāṇaśabdaravāṃś caiva śrutvā teṣāṃ mahātmanām
english: exultant, all their aims fulfilled, roaring on every side — and hearing too the sound and clamor of the arrows of those great-souled ones,

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja kaśmalenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ apayāne manaś cakre vihīnabalavāhanaḥ
english: Duryodhana, O great king, overcome by despair, his forces and his mount gone, set his mind upon flight.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca nihate māmake sainye niḥśeṣe śibire kṛte pāṇḍavānāṃ balaṃ sūta kiṃ nu śeṣam abhūt tadā etan me pṛcchato brūhi kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My army slain and left without remnant, my camp made desolate — what then, O charioteer, was the strength of the Pāṇḍavas that remained? Tell me this, who ask it of you, for you are skilled, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yac ca duryodhano mandaḥ kṛtavāṃs tanayo mama balakṣayaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā sa ekaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: And what did my dull-witted son Duryodhana do, that lord of the earth, alone, having beheld the ruin of his host in this way?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rathānāṃ dve sahasre tu sapta nāgaśatāni ca pañca cāśvasahasrāṇi pattīnāṃ ca śataṃ śatāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Two thousand chariots, and seven hundred elephants, and five thousand horse, and ten thousand foot —

sanskrit: etac cheṣam abhūd rājan pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam parigṛhya hi yad yuddhe dhṛṣṭadyumno vyavasthitaḥ
english: this was the great force of the Pāṇḍavas that remained, O king, having taken command of which Dhṛṣṭadyumna stood arrayed in the battle.

sanskrit: ekākī bharataśreṣṭha tato duryodhano nṛpaḥ nāpaśyat samare kaṃ cit sahāyaṃ rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, alone, O best of the Bhāratas, that foremost of chariot-warriors, saw no comrade anywhere in the battle.

sanskrit: nardamānān parāṃś caiva svabalasya ca saṃkṣayam hataṃ svahayam utsṛjya prāṅmukhaḥ prādravad bhayāt
english: Beholding the foes roaring and the destruction of his own host, he abandoned his slain horse and fled eastward in fear.
